scope: Optional one-dimensional Hamiltonian companion/time-field candidate with photon backreaction and conserved total energy and momentum. No claim of ordinary gravitons, a complete void model or observed agreement.
receiver: All energy lost by the photon packet enters this candidate companion field. Receiver selection is already fixed by the user's model.
field: Periodic real Fourier field n(x)>0. A homogeneous mode and sine/cosine modes have positive kinetic energy; nonzero modes have wave speed v. Finite packet coupling uses a translation-invariant Gaussian spatial smoothing.
controls: Zero initial rolling rate at 64 modes, inertia 1 and all three packet energies
Spatially translated packet at 64 modes, inertia 1, energy 0.01
No photon: homogeneous rolling energy is constant and traveling modes remain zero
required_outputs: Separate received energy into homogeneous-field gain and nonzero-wave energy
Record pre-existing companion-field energy rather than crediting it to photons
Show total momentum exchange, not only photon energy bookkeeping
Check positivity along the calculated solution
Compare intensity and inertia dependence and resolve finite-mode error
limits: Classical effective field/ray approximation. Gaussian smoothing is a declared finite-size coupling, not a derived ultraviolet completion. No expansion or gravitational clock-dilation premise. Matter clocks, atomic coupling, void localization, companion capture, lensing and permanent gravity deposits are not implemented. Periodic boundaries and the homogeneous rolling state are explicit model assumptions.
local_transport_followup: After inspecting the preliminary mode decomposition, add a full real-space energy-flux balance in the fixed interval X_initial +/-0.5. Include cross energy and flux against the initially rolling field. This diagnostic prevents interpreting nonzero mode energy as the entire transportable energy.
